newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore to spend $255 million on sports for all.
newsitem.headline: Singapore to spend $255 million on sports for all.

text.p: Singapore will spend S$360 million (US$255 million) over the next decade on programmes aimed at giving its three million residents easy access to sports, the Straits Times newspaper said on Monday.

It quoted Singapore Sports Council executive director Kwan Yue Yeong as saying: "With increased affluence, many Singaporeans have very unhealthy and sedentary lifestyles. They spend more time playing computer games, going to the movies or buffets."

A goal of the project is to help counter such unhealthy side-effects of the city-state's growing affluence by putting a swimming complex, indoor sports hall and running track within three km (two miles) of every resident.
The programme aims to double the percentage of Singaporeans who play a sport at least once a week from 24 percent now to 50 percent by 2005, the Straits Times said.
